name: Signed Note
description: The description as a short note from the person who made it, in first person, ending in a sign-off. No headers, no blocks, no boilerplate. For channels carried by one voice, where the description is part of the relationship rather than an index.
architecture: A short first-person note to the viewer, signed off at the end.

sections.instruction: Open the note in first person, as the person who made this episode addressing one reader. Say plainly why you made it — a reason drawn from the episode's own subject, not a generic one.
Say what the episode is and what happens in it, still in the same first-person voice. Do not switch into a blurb.
One short passage on something you noticed or had to leave out while making it. Only use what the story context supports; if it supports nothing, write about what surprised you in the subject itself.
Close the note in one or two sentences and sign off. Warm, brief, and without asking for a like or a subscription.
Emit only hashtags, on a single line, separated by spaces. No sentence, no heading, no commentary. At most four.

title_plan.guidance: Plain and personal, in the same first-person register as the note. No colon-subtitle construction and no branding suffix.

tag_plan.guidance: for this personal episode, staying close to the subject rather than the channel

constraints: First person throughout, one voice, no headers.
Never ask for a like, a subscription, or a comment.
Nothing about the making of it may be invented — only what the story context supports.
